scenario: Read the radio control pins in U-Boot. Transfer each diagnostic kernel to RAM over UART0 and check its CRC32. Boot with the board DTB and the microSD root. In the RF test, read both pins after root mount and record the first RF initialization attempt. Repeat the RF test after booting the vendor Linux station and verifying association and DHCP. Allow one more interval for the original calibration reply, then request MM_VERSION once. Repeat with the observed Linux command order and zero expected calibration parameter bytes. In the separate MAC test, query the MAC address and request a MAC reset without RF setup. After the calibration timeout, boot Luckfox Linux without removing power and scan again. For the handoff test, start the vendor station without loading network profiles or keys. Request a disconnect, terminate the supplicant and bring the wireless interface down. Check its state and USB driver binding. Reboot directly into the first-interface diagnostic kernel. Repeat the measured Linux command sequence after removal of board power and UART. On a separate boot of the same image, drive the WLAN enable signal low for at least 20 ms, then high for at least 20 ms before kernel entry. Boot the GENERIC kernel with the startup condition reads in RAM. Check the two factory condition labels, request two scans, and check the supplicant and IP addresses. For the clock and PMU tests, boot each kernel in RAM with the same board DTB. Check the initial selector and PMU variant. Record which of the 17 fixed requests receive matching confirmations. Repeat with the same requests and a driver that accepts either DENOM_UPDATE value in three divider confirmations. Check station attachment, two scans, IP configuration and direct SSH from the host. For the OEM comparison, observe the existing USB confirmations for steps 5, 6 and 7 during the first WLAN interface open. Reboot to the installed microSD after the report. On a separate EmberBSD RAM boot, require all 17 confirmations. Read the installed NAND station kit from the FFS root. Run the factory normal RF command sequence once and observe both USB inputs for 12 seconds during MM_SET_RF_CALIB.
expected: The radio returns the RF calibration confirmation. Initialization can then continue to station setup. In the handoff test, MM_START succeeds before the driver creates a station and starts a passive scan. The fixed clock and PMU sequence requires a confirmation for each of its 17 requests before station attachment.
observed: U-Boot read GPIO1_C5 as input high and GPIO1_C7 as input low. After root mount, EmberBSD read GPIO1_C5 (WL_DIS#) as input high and GPIO1_C7 (antenna select) as output high. MM_SET_STACK_START returned 0x007c with two bytes and the 5 GHz flag clear. MM_SET_TXPWR_IDX_LVL returned 0x0078 with zero bytes. Each MM_SET_RF_CONFIG command for TX0, TX1, RX20 and RX40 returned 0x0068 with zero bytes. MM_SET_RF_CALIB timed out after four seconds while waiting for 0x006a with 16 bytes. USB kept the radio attached during this capture. The driver stopped before station attachment and scan. Before the repeat, Luckfox Linux found 10 BSS entries, completed SAE association with PMF and CCMP, and obtained a DHCP lease. EmberBSD again received the stack, transmit power and four RF table confirmations. The original calibration request received no confirmation during either four-second interval. The single MM_VERSION query also timed out after four seconds. Both bulk IN endpoints returned zero valid configuration records in each of the three intervals. The radio remained attached throughout the capture. EmberBSD created no station interface. With the measured Linux sequence, the native driver received seven confirmations for stack start, firmware version, transmit power and four RF tables. It then waited for 0x006a with zero parameter bytes. Both four-second calibration waits expired. The single MM_VERSION query also timed out after four seconds. Both bulk IN endpoints reported zero configuration records during each interval. USB kept the radio attached. The kernel exposed no station interface. In the separate MAC test, MM_GET_MAC_ADDR returned 0x0074 with six bytes. MM_RESET reported INVAL while waiting for 0x0001 with zero bytes. The radio then detached and enumerated again. Linux recovered the radio without a power cycle. A fresh scan found 10 BSS entries, including one match for a saved network. In the separate handoff test, Linux completed the disconnect, supplicant shutdown and interface-down commands. Its only wireless interface was down. The aic8800_fdrv driver remained bound to interface 2 of a69c:88dc. After the software reboot, EmberBSD sent MM_START. Bulk IN endpoint 0x81 reported INVAL while the driver waited for confirmation 0x0003 with zero bytes. The radio disconnected and enumerated again. The driver skipped a second attempt on that USB port. Only lo0 appeared in single-user mode. Station creation and scan did not run. At cold start, GPIO1_C5 was an input at level 1. During the separate boot, U-Boot read back output levels 0 and 1. The kernel then read level 1 on the output. Both runs received the same seven confirmations. Neither received a calibration or version confirmation in the three four-second intervals. Both bulk IN endpoints returned zero valid configuration records in each interval. No station interface appeared. The GENERIC kernel sequenced WL_DIS# and identified chip 0x07, sub-ID 0x01. It reported factory USB setup skip and BBPLL setup skip (no CPU crystal). Both scans returned EIO. The radio rejected station creation with status 1. The supplicant remained disconnected. There was no IPv4 or routable IPv6 address. In the first two clock and PMU tests, the initial selector was zero and the driver selected the extended PMU mask. The radio confirmed both clock requests and the first two PMU requests. Both drivers stopped at step 5. Its confirmation declared eight parameter bytes and contained eight. The diagnostic kernel confirmed the register address and divider value. Only DENOM_UPDATE (0x80) differed among the selected bits. On the third RAM boot, the radio confirmed both clock settings and all 15 PMU settings. The driver checked the address and the divider bits in each of the three divider confirmations. The kernel attached aicwf0 at uaicfw0. Both scan commands returned EIO at station creation. Firmware returned status 1 to MM_ADD_IF. The supplicant reported DISCONNECTED. The interface had no IPv4 or routable IPv6 address. Both mdnsd and sshd were running. Direct SSH from the host stopped at name resolution. A subsequent boot of the same image through /boot.scr on microSD also received all 17 confirmations and attached aicwf0. In the separate 261020 RAM boot, the factory driver completed its first interface open. Each confirmation for steps 5, 6 and 7 echoed the requested address and reported divider 2 with DENOM_UPDATE clear. After the OEM run, the board booted the installed 2d7a76ae kernel from microSD and confirmed the full 17-command sequence again. In the post-PMU run, the radio confirmed stack start (2 parameter bytes), firmware version (64), transmit power (0) and each of four RF configurations (0). MM_SET_RF_CALIB timed out. Both USB inputs reported zero configuration records during its 12-second wait. The driver stopped before station attachment.
limits: The PCB revision is unknown. The binaries are diagnostic builds. The GPIO values describe the two sampling points.
The Linux interface state and USB driver binding were observed on the host. Firmware acknowledgement of interface shutdown and the causes of the native timeouts and USB disconnects remain unknown.
EmberBSD beacon reception, association, DHCP and SSH over Wi-Fi remain unverified.
GPIO1_C5 controls WL_DIS#. These level observations do not measure the radio supply rail or its internal reset state.

The two startup labels describe the conditional branches in the factory USB and clock setup on this radio. They do not measure clock frequency or completion of the subsequent factory clock, power, patch or DPD stages.

The OEM observer reported fields in the returned confirmation words. It issued no radio commands. The cause and timing of the DENOM_UPDATE difference remain unknown. The 17 accepted native confirmations establish completion of the command sequence. Clock frequency, supply voltage, PLL lock and DPD state were outside this measurement.
The post-PMU run issued the late RF request. It did not load the WLAN patch or run the early DPD program. The timeout does not identify which early operation the radio requires.
